extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, magazine editors, and entrants/submission-curators for the O. Henry Prize
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and process used by the O. Henry Prize series and guest editors to select twenty short stories each year; emphasizes editorial philosophy, qualities sought in stories, eligibility, and curation process. Useful for authors aiming to understand what kinds of stories are likely to be noticed and chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial philosophy — no fixed criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: "The editor has no set criteria nor does she look for something specific in the many short stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories aren't required to have certain kinds of characters, settings, plots, voices, or styles; openness rather than checklist-driven selection is the operating principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary hope: emotional and revelatory impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "To be moved by stories that feel new and tell something readers didn't know or make them aware of something they knew but wouldn't acknowledge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors stories that move the reader and provide either genuine new information/insight or articulate an overlooked or unacknowledged truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness
rubrics_metrics.description: - **Newness** — feels like something not read before
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for material, perspectives, or approaches that feel fresh or surprising rather than derivative or overly familiar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revelation
rubrics_metrics.description: - **Revelation** — illuminates something previously unknown OR articulates something readers know but won't admit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that disclose, clarify, or give language to overlooked aspects of experience are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affective resonance—stories that provoke feeling or disturb complacency—counts strongly toward selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No formula / radical openness to form
rubrics_metrics.description: - **No formula** — radical openness to form, voice, perspective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor explicitly resists formulaic expectations; innovative forms, voices, and perspectives are welcomed rather than penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process: broad reading and curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Series editor reads broadly across magazines and online and forwards a curated long-list to a guest editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is a two-stage curation: broad discovery by the series editor, then final selection by a guest editor; implies importance of visibility in magazines and online venues the series editor monitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final selection by guest editor (discretionary taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest editor selects 20 prize stories per year; each guest editor has unique vision reflected in selections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because guest editors bring distinct tastes, what succeeds can vary year-to-year; there is no single stable template beyond the editorial philosophy of novelty and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publication venue and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories published in U.S. and Canadian magazines (now also translation-eligible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered, stories must appear in eligible magazines (U.S./Canada) or be qualifying translations; publication in those venues is a prerequisite for consideration.
